# PixelProvenance agent contract

Version: 0.2.0
Event: `pixelprovenance:package`
Toolbar default: on for localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1]; off elsewhere unless `data-pp-enabled="true"` or `enabled: true`.

## What to install

Prefer the drop-in. It paints a Select/Crop toolbar, tags `[data-pp]` with the chroma signal, and emits a selection package. React `DevTag` is optional for apps that want wrapper components instead of attributes. The CLI decoder is optional and used for PNG files plus a codebook JSON, not for the default toolbar flow.

Do not auto-tag every `div`. Do not enable the overlay in production builds unless the user asked for that.

## Package install

1. `npm view pixelprovenance version` — if it exists, `npm install pixelprovenance`.
2. Else `npm install github:jasonkneen/pixelprovenance` (or the host's package manager equivalent).
3. Else pack a local checkout: `npm pack` in this repo, then `npm install /path/to/pixelprovenance-0.2.0.tgz`.

Peer: React 18 or 19 only if using `DevTag`. Node >= 20.19 for the CLI. The IIFE drop-in has no React peer.

After install, `node_modules/pixelprovenance/dist/pixelprovenance-dropin.js` must exist. If it is missing, run `npm run build:lib` in the package (git installs run `prepare` → `build:lib`).

## Drop-in (default)

### Script tag

```html
<script
  src="/pixelprovenance-dropin.js"
  data-pp-page="pricing"
  data-pp-endpoint="http://127.0.0.1:8787/package"
></script>
```

Copy `dist/pixelprovenance-dropin.js` into the host `public/` directory, or point `src` at the file under `node_modules` if the bundler serves it.

### Bundler

```ts
import { mount } from 'pixelprovenance/dropin'

mount({
  pageId: 'pricing',
  endpoint: 'http://127.0.0.1:8787/package',
  enabled: import.meta.env.DEV,
})
```

Mount once from a client-only root. Next.js: `'use client'` wrapper. Do not import this module from a Server Component.

### Script attributes (`data-pp-*` on the script tag)

| Attribute | Maps to | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `data-pp-page` | `pageId` | `page` |
| `data-pp-endpoint` | POST URL | none |
| `data-pp-enabled` | `true` / `false` | loopback on, else off |
| `data-pp-intensity` | carrier opacity: alpha = round(intensity × 50)/255 | `0.06` (3/255 ≈ 1%) |
| `data-pp-pattern-size` | default CSS tile 16–256 | `64` |
| `data-pp-debug` | `true` outlines each carrier | `false` |
| `data-pp-verify-pixels` | `true` also decodes crop pixels in-page | `false` |

### Region attributes (on host markup)

| Attribute | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `data-pp` | Stable path segment. Required for a named region. |
| `data-pp-type` | Category in the seed. Default: tag name. |
| `data-pp-source` | `file:line:column` hashed into the pattern. |
| `data-pp-key` | Stable key for repeated items: `row[<key>]`. |
| `data-pp-pattern-size` | Override the tile. Default is automatic: the page default, or 32 when the element's shorter side is under 1.5 tiles. Avoid 16 (resampling blurs it). |

Nested `data-pp` builds `pageId/parent/child`. Same-name siblings under one tagged parent get `name[0]`, `name[1]`… in document order, so list rows get distinct carriers; add `data-pp-key` when order changes. Click target: deepest `[data-pp]`, else `[data-testid]`, else `[id]`, else the element. The toolbar is marked `data-pp-toolbar` and is not selectable.

### Carrier layer

Carriers are painted into one overlay layer (`[data-pp-signal-layer]`, a child of `<body>`), positioned over each tag and clipped by `overflow` ancestors. Host elements are never restyled or given children, so `<img>`/`<input>` tags work and framework reconciliation is untouched. A MutationObserver, ResizeObserver and scroll/resize listeners keep it in step with tags added or moved after mount. Nodes that already have a React `DevTag` signal child are skipped.

### Global API

After mount, `window.PixelProvenance` has `mount`, `unmount`, `select`, `crop`, `cancel`, `onPackage(cb)`, `exportRegistry()`.

`onPackage` is also `import { deliverPackage } from 'pixelprovenance/dropin'` → `deliverPackage.subscribe`.

## Selection package

`version` is the literal `1`. HTML is truncated to 4000 characters.

Crop packages add `method`:

- `dom` — layout names the subject: the best-overlap tag among those covering ≥ 50% of the crop. `candidates` lists up to five overlapping tags with `coverage` and `iou`. With `verifyPixels`, `pixel: { path, score, agrees }` reports the in-page pixel decode.
- `pixels` — no tag covers the crop, and the pixel decode named one; `score` is its correlation.
- `none` — nothing matched; `path` is `<pageId>/crop`.

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "pageId": "pricing",
  "path": "pricing/plan-card/cta",
  "type": "button",
  "depth": 3,
  "selector": "[data-pp=\"cta\"]",
  "rect": { "x": 80, "y": 420, "w": 160, "h": 44 },
  "source": { "file": "src/Pricing.tsx", "line": 88, "column": 9 },
  "html": "<button data-pp=\"cta\">Start</button>",
  "image": "data:image/png;base64,...",
  "capturedAt": "2026-09-08T00:00:00.000Z"
}
```

Delivery order:

1. `window` event `pixelprovenance:package` (`event.detail` is the object)
2. `POST` to `endpoint` with `Content-Type: application/json` if set
3. `onPackage` subscribers

A model should consume this JSON. Do not ask the model to decode the frequency pattern.

### Reference receiver

```bash
npx pixelprovenance-receive --port 8787 --out .pixelprovenance/inbox
```

`POST /package` stores `<time>-<path>.json` plus `.png` and `latest.json`, and prints `path  file:line`. `GET /latest` returns the newest package without the image. It answers the CORS and Private Network Access preflight a page on another localhost port sends. Also importable: `import { createReceiver } from 'pixelprovenance/receive'`.

## cluso-inspector plugin

When the host already runs cluso-inspector, add PixelProvenance as a plugin instead of a second toolbar:

```html
<script src="/pixelprovenance-cluso.js" data-pp-page="pricing"></script>
<script src="/cluso-inspector.js" data-auto data-endpoint="http://localhost:4747/annotations"></script>
```

Order does not matter. Or `import { pixelprovenancePlugin } from 'pixelprovenance/cluso'` and `ClusoInspector.use(pixelprovenancePlugin(), { pageId: 'pricing' })`. The plugin paints carriers while the inspector is enabled (toolbar toggle), adds `pixelprovenance: { path, type, source }` plus a Markdown line to each comment target, fills `target.source` from `data-pp-source` when the framework gave none, names the tagged subject of region comments, and attaches `payload.pixelprovenance.registry` so an agent can decode any screenshot of the page.

## React tags (optional)

```tsx
import { DevTag, DevTagRoot } from 'pixelprovenance'

<DevTagRoot pageId="DASHBOARD" enabled={import.meta.env.DEV}>
  <DevTag id="card" type="panel" source={{ file: 'src/Dashboard.tsx', line: 8, column: 9 }}>
    <Card />
  </DevTag>
</DevTagRoot>
```

`source` is part of the pattern seed. A CLI codebook must repeat the same path, type, depth, and source. Drop-in will not double-paint a node that already has a DevTag signal child.

## Decoder CLI (optional)

```bash
pixelprovenance-decode screenshot.png --registry components.json --json
```

`--registry` is required. Exit 0 on match, 1 on no match or error. JSON no-match is `[]`.

Carriers are pattern v2 by default: twelve 2-D waves decoded shift-invariantly (fold modulo the tile, DFT at the known bins). Default threshold is 0.5 for v2 (true matches ≥ ~0.6, unrelated tags ≤ ~0.4) and 0.7 when the registry contains v1 entries. Screenshots made before v2 decode with `--pattern-version 1` or `"patternVersion": 1` per registry entry. The cluso plugin's `payload.pixelprovenance.registry` is a ready-made registry.

Tiny controls (under ~48px on a side) hold too few carrier pixels to decode reliably from a screenshot; in-page Select/Crop name them from layout instead.

## Verify

On localhost:

1. Toolbar shows Select, Crop, Cancel.
2. Select → click a `[data-pp]` node.
3. A `pixelprovenance:package` event fires with the expected `path`.
4. Crop a region inside a tag → `method: "dom"` and that tag's `path`.
5. If `endpoint` is set, the POST body is that object (`npx pixelprovenance-receive` prints it).

Host tests: keep the overlay behind the host dev flag.

## Out of scope unless asked

MCP server, SSE worker, npm publish, auto-tagging the whole DOM, production-on-by-default.
